project.title: Investment Committee Simulation
project.subtitle: Three approval gates. Four committee members. One integrated recommendation.
project.premise: Your four-person investment committee advises three client mandates and manages $500,000 in hypothetical assets. The committee must establish a market view, build and challenge each portfolio, and defend one evidence-linked recommendation.
project.scopeNote: Canvas remains the authority for due dates, submission links, and course-grade weights.

roles.title: Client and Macro Strategist
roles.mandate: Own client discovery, the 12-month market view, IPS objectives and constraints, and the handoff from client needs to investment criteria.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Lead the client interview, document goals and RRTTLLU constraints, establish the macro context, and name unresolved information gaps.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Test whether proposed allocations and securities fit the approved client mandate and the committee's market view.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: Defend client suitability, the macro assumptions, and the line from discovered need to recommendation.

roles.title: Fixed-Income Analyst
roles.mandate: Own the income, capital-preservation, maturity, duration, credit-quality, liquidity, and tax questions that shape the fixed-income sleeve.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Translate cash-flow needs, time horizon, liquidity, taxes, and loss capacity into fixed-income questions and provisional guardrails.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Analyze yields, duration, credit, liquidity, and structure; recommend fixed-income exposures that meet the approved guardrails.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: Defend the portfolio's income, capital-preservation, interest-rate, and credit-risk trade-offs.

roles.title: Fund and ETF Analyst
roles.mandate: Own pooled-vehicle due diligence, diversification, benchmark fit, fees, liquidity, tax considerations, and active-versus-passive implementation.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Identify the client's diversification, access, liquidity, cost, tax, values, and vehicle requirements before screening products.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Evaluate funds and ETFs using objective, holdings, benchmark, fees, liquidity, tax efficiency, and tracking evidence.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: Defend vehicle selection, implementation feasibility, diversification, and product-level due diligence.

roles.title: Portfolio Manager and Risk Analyst
roles.mandate: Own portfolio integration, risk capacity versus willingness, the drawdown tripwire, decision-log quality, stress testing, and mandate-breach escalation.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Reconcile risk capacity and willingness, set provisional portfolio guardrails, challenge assumptions, and audit the Analyst Decision Log.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Integrate the allocation, run bear-case stress tests, compare mitigants, identify breaches, and require corrective action.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: State the integrated recommendation, present the strongest downside case, and lead preparation for adversarial Q&A.

committeeProtocol.description: Circulate the required evidence before the meeting. Every member reviews the full package.
The workstream lead states a clear recommendation and cites the evidence that supports it.
The Portfolio Manager and Risk Analyst coordinates the strongest counterargument; the analyst whose judgment is challenged must respond with evidence.
The phase lead states the motion. The Portfolio Manager and Risk Analyst records approve, revise, or reject; all four members vote and ties require revision.
Capture evidence reviewed, dissent or reservations, owners, and actions before the next gate.

phase1Experience.title: Client Discovery and AI Decision Protocol
phase1Experience.subtitle: Interview the client. Challenge the first answer. Verify the evidence. Set the guardrails.
phase1Experience.purpose: Turn a fictional client profile into documented investment criteria before the team screens a bond, mutual fund, ETF, or portfolio allocation.

clientSets.inquiry: Investigate how near-term spending, concentrated wealth, and overlapping goals change the meaning of risk.
Investigate how illiquidity, taxes, a known cash need, and retirement urgency constrain an otherwise attractive return target.
Investigate how experience, values, variable income, and emergency reserves affect capacity, willingness, and product fit.
Investigate how loss aversion, currency exposure, relocation, taxes, and restricted holdings affect implementable choices.
Investigate how philanthropy, debt, uneven cash flow, starting capital, and multigenerational goals change portfolio priorities.

interviewPrototype.label: Client Option 1 · Controlled prototype

portrait.alt: Fictional portrait of Eleanor Vance, an older woman with silver hair and glasses in a softly lit library setting.
portrait.caption: AI-generated fictional portrait for this classroom simulation; not a real client.

interviewPrototype.voiceCue: Simulation voice: thoughtful, measured, and cautious. Eleanor acknowledges uncertainty instead of filling gaps. This cue shapes delivery, not case evidence.
interviewPrototype.greeting: Hello. I’m Eleanor Vance. I understand you want to learn what matters before your committee makes any decisions. I may need you to narrow a question, and if the case does not establish an answer, I’ll say so.
acknowledgements: That is a useful place to start.
I see why you are asking.
Let me separate what I know from what I do not.
That question gets closer to the decision I am worried about.

clarificationResponses.risk: When you say risk, are you asking how I feel about a loss or how much loss my financial situation could absorb? Those are not the same question.
clarificationResponses.general: Could you narrow that question to one decision-relevant area—goals, cash flow, timing, liquidity, risk, resources, taxes, holdings, family needs, or values?

interviewPrototype.boundary: The intake card is intentionally incomplete. Responses follow the same instructor-approved paths for every student, disclose a case fact only after a materially relevant question, mark unsupported details as information gaps, and never recommend investments.

visibleDossier.label: Still to discover
visibleDossier.value: Cash needs, timing, resources, risk context, and unique constraints

scenarioFacts.liquidityNeed: high liquidity needs for medical expenses

openingQuestions: What matters most to you about this portfolio?
What cash needs could change the plan?
How soon might you need access to the money?
What would make an investment loss difficult for you?

responses: I keep coming back to two things: I want the savings protected, and I want it to help provide income. I am not sure which concern should dominate if they conflict.
Preservation and income are still the headline. The difficult part is deciding what has to come first when another need competes with them.
followUpResponses: By preservation, I mean avoiding a result that puts an important near-term need at risk. The case does not establish a precise acceptable loss, so that remains a question for your team to frame carefully.
dialoguePaths.followUpQuestion: Would it help if you asked what could force me to use the money sooner?

responses: There is a medical-spending concern behind my need for liquidity. Access matters, but I cannot give you an amount or exact date because the case does not establish either one.
I do need funds kept accessible for medical expenses. I hesitate to be more specific—the amount, frequency, and timing are all still information gaps.
followUpResponses: That is exactly where the brief stops: the medical liquidity need is high, but no dollar amount or payment date is established. Please do not turn that uncertainty into an invented number.
dialoguePaths.followUpQuestion: Do you want to separate what is known about that cash need from the amount and timing that are still missing?

responses: My documented income is {{annualIncome}}. Whether that pension covers ordinary spending or medical costs is not established.
The one dependable cash-flow fact in the file is {{annualIncome}}. I cannot tell you my spending level or any shortfall from the approved facts.
followUpResponses: I can confirm {{annualIncome}}, but the case gives no expense budget. You still cannot calculate investable surplus or a required distribution from that number alone.
dialoguePaths.followUpQuestion: Would you like to ask what that income does—and does not—tell you about my spending or distribution need?

responses: The approved horizon is {{horizon}}. That range is wider than I would like, and the file does not tell us where inside it the need is most likely to fall.
I can narrow the planning window to {{horizon}}, but not to a single date. That uncertainty is part of the decision, not permission to pick the midpoint.
followUpResponses: No, the case does not identify a more precise date than {{horizon}}. Your record should preserve that range and the uncertainty around it.
dialoguePaths.followUpQuestion: What other need would you want to connect to that time window?

responses: The case lists my net worth as {{netWorth}}. It does not say how much is investable, liquid, or already committed.
My documented net worth is {{netWorth}}, but that total alone does not tell you what can safely be allocated or withdrawn.
followUpResponses: I cannot break the {{netWorth}} into cash, securities, property, or other holdings because the approved scenario does not provide that allocation.
dialoguePaths.followUpQuestion: Would you treat net worth as investable cash, or is there another question you need to ask first?

responses: I would describe myself as cautious—the case classifies me as {{riskClassification}}. But it does not establish how I would react to a specific percentage loss.
I am uneasy with loss, which is consistent with the {{riskClassification}} classification. I cannot honestly give you a precise drawdown limit from the facts provided.
followUpResponses: The file still does not establish a loss threshold or a past reaction to volatility. Treat willingness as cautious, but do not manufacture a percentage.
dialoguePaths.followUpQuestion: Are you also going to ask whether my finances can bear a loss, rather than only how I feel about one?

responses: My capacity is not answered by one number. The case gives a short planning window and a medical liquidity need, but it does not quantify the liability, so I would be careful about claiming I can absorb a loss.
I have resources, but the need for accessible medical funds complicates capacity. Without the amount and timing, the file does not support a precise loss capacity.
followUpResponses: The unresolved medical amount is what prevents a confident capacity estimate. Net worth, income, and timing need to be considered together rather than used as substitutes for one another.
dialoguePaths.followUpQuestion: Which missing cash-need fact would you need before setting a defensible risk limit?

responses: The case file lists expected return {{expectedReturn}}, standard deviation {{standardDeviation}}, and risk-aversion score {{riskAversionScore}}. Those are scenario inputs, not my recommendation or proof that a portfolio is suitable.

The approved metrics are E(R) {{expectedReturn}}, standard deviation {{standardDeviation}}, and risk aversion {{riskAversionScore}}. You still need to reconcile them with the actual goal, liquidity need, and horizon.
followUpResponses: I cannot explain how those case metrics were derived because the scenario does not provide that methodology. Verify how your team uses them rather than treating them as self-justifying.

responses: I do not want to guess about taxes. The approved case gives no tax bracket, account type, or tax restriction, so all three are information gaps.
Nothing in the scenario establishes my tax status or account registration. Please record that instead of assuming a taxable or retirement account.
followUpResponses: There is no additional approved tax fact to disclose. The investment impact may be material, but the correct interview result is still ‘not established.’

responses: My current holdings are not in the approved brief. You should not infer a stock, bond, cash, or fund allocation from my net worth.
I cannot give you an existing portfolio because the case does not establish one. Record holdings and concentration as unresolved before evaluating a transition plan.
followUpResponses: No specific security, account, cost basis, or concentration is approved for this case. That remains a material information gap.

responses: The scenario does not identify dependents, beneficiaries, heirs, or a legacy objective. I would rather leave that unanswered than invent a family situation.
No family or beneficiary need is established in my brief. It could change the plan, but it must stay on the information-gap list.
followUpResponses: There is no approved follow-up fact about family, estate, or beneficiaries. Your analysis should show the uncertainty without filling it in.

responses: The approved facts do not establish an ethical screen, religious restriction, or other values-based exclusion for me.
I cannot add a values preference that is not in the case. Record values and unique restrictions as not established.
followUpResponses: No additional values or unique-constraint fact is approved. The absence of a fact is not evidence that I have no preference; it is an information gap.

responses: I am 72 and retired after working as a librarian. The financial details that matter still depend on what you ask next.
My intake information identifies me as a 72-year-old retired librarian. I would rather discuss one planning issue at a time than have you infer the rest from my age.
followUpResponses: That is the full approved background: age 72 and retired librarian. No additional biography is established.

complication.response: I should clarify something because it changes the order of my priorities: when I say preservation and income, I do not mean tying up money I may need for medical expenses. If that need arrives sooner than expected, access comes before seeking more income.
complication.responseWithHorizon: I should clarify something because it changes the order of my priorities: within that {{horizon}} window, access for medical expenses comes before seeking more income. Preservation cannot mean tying up money I may need.
complication.recordPrompt: This is the complication to carry forward: liquidity may override the income objective, while the amount and timing remain unresolved.

broadResponses: That is a broad question, and I do not want to make up a complete story. Please narrow it to goals, cash flow, timing, liquidity, risk, resources, taxes, holdings, family needs, or values.
I can answer from the approved brief, but only one issue at a time. Which decision-relevant area do you want to clarify first?
unknownResponses: I cannot answer that from the approved brief. Please record it as an information gap rather than treating my hesitation as a fact.
That detail is not established in the case. It may matter, but your Decision Record should show it as unresolved.
I do not have an approved fact for that question. Please do not infer an answer from the other information I have shared.
recommendationResponses: I cannot choose a security, fund, ETF, bond, or portfolio weight for you. Ask me about my needs or constraints; your team must verify the evidence and make the investment decision.
That would turn the interview into a recommendation. I can clarify priorities and information gaps, but I cannot tell you what to buy, sell, or allocate.

decisionCycle.action: Before any AI interaction, the team records one tentative, evidence-based interpretation for each assigned client: what the client needs, which constraints matter, and the preliminary investment implications.
decisionCycle.logEvidence: The interpretation; supporting case evidence and assumptions; unanswered questions; and the portfolio or security decision it could affect

decisionCycle.action: Use the bounded role-play prompt. Ask open, neutral questions; mark any answer not established by the case as unknown.
decisionCycle.logEvidence: Prompt purpose and output summary—not a pasted transcript

decisionCycle.action: Ask AI for the strongest counterinterpretation, hidden assumption, and missing downside—not for the final recommendation.
decisionCycle.logEvidence: Material challenge and the claim that now requires checking

decisionCycle.action: Verify client facts in the assigned files, calculations in the team workbook, and external claims in an approved source with an as-of date.
decisionCycle.logEvidence: Source, link or file location, source date, and Confirmed / Qualified / Contradicted / Not verifiable

decisionCycle.action: State what changed, what remains uncertain, the final judgment, and the guardrail that later security selection or portfolio construction must honor.
decisionCycle.logEvidence: Final decision, concise rationale, downstream guardrail, and peer review

rolePlayPrompt: You are role-playing [CLIENT NAME], a fictional client in a BUS331 investment-analysis simulation.
Use only the facts inside the CLIENT BRIEF below. If the brief does not establish an answer, say: Not established—record this as an information gap.
Stay in the client's first-person voice. Do not recommend securities, mutual funds, ETFs, asset weights, or a risk score. Do not invent preferences, numbers, life events, sources, or certainty.
Answer one neutral interview question at a time. When the analyst asks about a trade-off, explain the client's stated priorities and the missing fact needed to decide.
CLIENT BRIEF: [paste only the assigned fictional profile facts from the public course files]
challengerPrompts: What is the strongest reasonable interpretation that contradicts our initial judgment? Separate case facts from assumptions.
Which client answer may reflect willingness to take risk but not financial capacity—or the reverse? What evidence would resolve the conflict?
Which claim, number, or product characteristic cannot be accepted until a human checks an approved source?
How could this proposed guardrail fail to protect the client's most important goal in a bear case?
What later bond, mutual-fund/ETF, or allocation decision would change if this assumption is wrong?

cfaFoundations.application: Understand the client's objectives and constraints before asset allocation and security analysis.
Connect business-cycle and macroeconomic conditions to the client's decision context without treating forecasts as facts.
Use cash-flow features, yield measures, interest-rate risk, liquidity, and credit analysis to frame later bond decisions.
Compare mutual funds and ETFs as implementation vehicles and examine diversification, benchmark, cost, liquidity, and fit.
Separate risk capacity from willingness, document a reasonable basis, challenge uncertainty, and preserve client-first reasoning.

decisionLogFields: Case fact, assumption, or market claim
qualityGate: Each role records at least one human-first judgment for each assigned client before using AI.
Every material AI challenge is summarized in the Analyst Decision Log; raw transcripts are not a substitute for analysis.
Every factual claim or number used in the final reasoning has an approved source and as-of date.
Unknown client information remains labeled unknown; it is not filled with invented AI detail.
The final reasoning states whether AI changed the judgment and why.
Each final judgment creates a testable guardrail for later fixed-income, mutual-fund/ETF, allocation, or risk decisions.
A second team member reviews the evidence trail before the Phase 1 gate.

phases.title: Frame the Mandate
phases.tagline: Agree on the world you are investing in and the rules you cannot break.
phases.keyQuestion: What must be true about markets and each client before we are willing to invest?
phases.objective: Establish one defensible 12-month market view and convert each assigned client profile into an approved investment mandate.
phases.gate: Approve or revise the common market view and all three client mandates. Portfolio construction cannot begin until the vote and action items are recorded.
phases.meetingMotion: Motion to approve the committee's market view and the investment mandate for each assigned client.

workstreams.title: Market view
workstreams.description: Read the historical data before using AI, compare the committee view with FactSet/FRED consensus, and build bull/base/bear scenarios.

workstreams.title: Client discovery
workstreams.description: Make a human-first judgment, interview the fictional client through the bounded AI protocol, and translate verified needs into RRTTLLU constraints.

workstreams.title: Decision log and guardrails
workstreams.description: Use AI to challenge the initial view, verify material claims, record final reasoning, and set criteria for later bonds, mutual funds/ETFs, allocation, and risk.

evidence: Human-first five-year macro read with source dates
FactSet/FRED consensus comparison and team forecast
Bull/base/bear scenarios with probabilities totaling 100%
RRTTLLU analysis for all three assigned clients
Return target, maximum volatility, and drawdown tripwire for each client
Analyst Decision Log showing initial judgment, AI challenge, verification, final reasoning, and downstream guardrail
Phase 1 decision record signed by all four members
deliverables: Completed Analyst Decision Log for all three assigned clients

phases.title: Build & Challenge
phases.tagline: Turn the approved view into portfolios, then try to break them.
phases.keyQuestion: Does each portfolio earn its place inside the client mandate after costs, constraints, and the bear case?
phases.objective: Translate the Phase 1 view into capital-market expectations, construct client portfolios, select securities, design risk mitigation, and challenge each recommendation under stress.
phases.gate: Approve, revise, or reject each client portfolio. A failed tripwire cannot receive approval without a documented correction.
phases.meetingMotion: Motion to approve the proposed portfolio and risk-mitigation plan for each assigned client.

workstreams.title: A · Capital-market expectations
workstreams.description: Convert the market view into expected returns, volatility, correlations, and Solver constraints for base and bear cases.

workstreams.title: B · Securities & implementation
workstreams.description: Select and weight securities, document macro and client fit, and compare at least two risk-mitigation approaches.

workstreams.title: C · Stress test & corrective action
workstreams.description: Run the bear case, test the tripwire, quantify hedge effects, and document trades required to cure any breach.

evidence: Base and bear CME inputs with cited rationale
Solver output and constraint checks for each client
Security-selection table with macro connection, client fit, weight, and source
Risk-mitigation comparison showing cost and trade-offs
Stress-test result against each approved tripwire
Before/after record for any corrective trades
AI audit entries linked to human verification
Phase 2 decision record signed by all four members
deliverables: Phase 2 decision record with client-by-client votes

phases.title: Defend the Recommendation
phases.tagline: Make the recommendation visible, auditable, and defensible under pressure.
phases.keyQuestion: Can every committee member defend the same evidence-linked recommendation to the panel?
phases.objective: Integrate the committee's work into a concise decision package and defend the client recommendations before an investment-committee panel.
phases.gate: Issue the final recommendation, record dissent or reservations, and defend the evidence. Every member must answer questions outside the workstream they led.
phases.meetingMotion: Motion to issue the committee's final recommendation and implementation plan for all assigned clients.

workstreams.title: Decision memo

workstreams.title: Technical exhibit book

workstreams.title: Committee defense
workstreams.description: Deliver a visual pitch, answer adversarial questions, and show that all four members understand the integrated decision.

evidence: Executive recommendation and decision memo

assessment.note: Canvas remains the authority for due dates, submission mechanics, and the project's course-grade weight. The criteria below preserve the existing written/oral assessment emphasis while aligning it to Phase 3.

writtenCriteria.standard: Calculations, formulas, sources, and portfolio metrics are correct, traceable, and interpreted.
The market view visibly drives CME assumptions, portfolio weights, securities, and client recommendations.
Each portfolio is tested against its tripwire; breaches trigger documented corrective action.
Exhibits communicate the decision clearly and include complete sources and the AI audit.
RRTTLLU constraints change the actual portfolio rather than appearing as generic narrative.

oralCriteria.standard: The committee tells one coherent story from market view to client action.
Members defend the base case, bear case, trade-offs, and quantitative evidence under questioning.
The team speaks as advisors to the committee with confident, concise, client-aware language.
All four members contribute, transition cleanly, and can answer beyond their lead workstream.
Slides make the recommendation and key evidence visible at a glance rather than serving as a script.
